newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ifo - rapid economic growth needed to create jobs.
newsitem.headline: Ifo - rapid economic growth needed to create jobs.

text.p: Ifo economic institute president Karl Heinrich Oppenlaender said on Thursday Germany would need annual growth rates of three to four percent in order to have any impact on its high jobless level.

Asked at a conference on economic issues to estimate how fast the German economy would have to grow to impact joblessness, he said: "It would have to be three to four percent to do anything about this situation."
Oppenlaender added that he did not expect that Germany can achieve its stated goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000. "I cannot imagine this at all," he said.
DIW institute chief economist Reiner Flassbeck, also attending the conference, agreed that the German jobless reduction goal was unrealistic.
"You have to think that the best ever result we have had in one year was to cut joblessness by 200,000," he said.
